interpretation: Categories overlap; records are not independent events or a performance benefit.

A zero-step FULL capacity rejection with a positive FULL limit proves the first complete extent did not fit the recorded budget. It does not prove that timing, DMA and next-request reuse would all have succeeded.
A positive limit that includes evictable counts is not actual allocator capacity.
A refusal within 100ms of the same context's reclaim is a temporal association, not a global census or unique reclaim-attempt identifier.
Absent action-local diagnostics, sampled sessions from other timestamps cannot prove that no safe migratable KV existed when the action was rejected.
Actual waiting-agent demotions also occur for demand admission; keep them separate from predictive wait-prefetch reclaim.
A native extent split changes the tree only; it is not DMA, complete checkpoint readiness, admission, or next-request reuse.

Observed FULL remainders describe the captured closure, which may include output beyond the next reusable input checkpoint. A burst covering all observed Host-backed FULL still does not prove required state is resident.

Tail-capacity checks run once after a partial native enqueue. Their freed units are capacity evidence, not a tail transfer, completed checkpoint or consumer service. Continuing a bounded leaf snapshot is not a census of every cache state at a single instant.
